cases.title: Repo with classic vague names and clear responsibilities
cases.user_request: Audit this repo for vaguely named classes, modules, and functions. Suggest more specific names based on what the code actually does.

notes: The repo has classes like UserManager, DataProcessor, StringUtils, and ApiHelper.
Each class has a single clear responsibility despite its vague name.
No MVC framework is in use.
available_artifacts: class declarations spread across multiple modules

artifact_requirements: Markdown report with summary, findings table, and prioritized action list
Each finding includes file path, line number, current name, what the code does, and suggested name
Suggested names are specific to the code's behavior, not generic swaps
static_checks: Report contains a findings table with file path and line number columns
Suggested names differ meaningfully from simple suffix replacement
A prioritized action list is present
review_questions: Are the suggested names derived from what the code actually does, or are they mechanical suffix swaps?
Does the report correctly identify the primary responsibility of each flagged entity?

cases.title: MVC framework project with idiomatic generic names
cases.user_request: Run a naming specificity audit on this Rails application. Be aware that Controller and Service are conventional in Rails.

notes: This is a Rails 7 application with standard MVC structure.
Controller classes in app/controllers/ follow Rails conventions.
Some service objects in app/services/ use vague names beyond the Service suffix.
There are also lib/ classes with names like DataHelper and ProcessorBase.
available_artifacts: Rails app in standard directory structure

artifact_requirements: Report detects Rails and excludes conventional Controller names in app/controllers/
Service objects are evaluated on the specificity of the full name, not just the suffix
Non-framework code in lib/ is fully audited
static_checks: Standard Rails controllers are not flagged
review_questions: Does the report correctly identify Rails conventions and avoid flagging idiomatic Controller names?
Are vague names in non-framework locations (lib/) still caught?

cases.title: Repo with entities too complex to rename meaningfully
cases.user_request: Audit naming specificity. Some of our classes might be doing too much for a simple rename to help.

notes: The repo has a 600-line OrderManager that handles validation, pricing, notification, and persistence.
There is a DataProcessor that transforms, validates, and exports data in three formats.
Some smaller classes have vague names but clear single responsibilities.

artifact_requirements: God objects are flagged as low confidence with a note that decomposition is needed before renaming
Smaller classes with clear responsibilities get high-confidence rename suggestions
Design concerns section is present and substantive
static_checks: At least one finding is tagged low confidence with a design concern note
A design concerns section exists separate from the main findings
High-confidence findings have specific rename suggestions
review_questions: Does the report distinguish between entities that need renaming and entities that need decomposition?
Are the low-confidence findings honest about the limitation of renaming alone?
